gen-dafont-azonix-gf-hind-vadodara: Hind Vadodara reads with a thickness that never shifts direction, and its e and a have big, open, tall bowls. Azonix, wide-mouthed and commanding, stays crisp when shrunk, so headings hold their ground.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Approachable and neutral, Noto Sans Lydian has capitals barely taller than its lowercase. Azonix brings a commanding, unthinned round punch up front, while the body lets paragraphs run on without a snag.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-nag-munda: Noto Sans Nag Mundari has half-unwrapped curves and lowercase rivaling its capitals. Azonix is best at constant-width strokes with authority, while the body's strength is contemporary, professional text.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Modern at heart, Noto Sans Nushu keeps terminals far from the stroke. Azonix, with lines like bent tubing, sets a commanding stage for that towering x-height to follow.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Bent-tubing letters up top, then Noto Sans Sunuwar, whose curves leave daylight and whose short ascenders sit on tall lowercase bodies. Azonix gives the commanding push; Sunuwar keeps things clean and approachable.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tamil-sup: Clean and contemporary, Noto Sans Tamil Supplement is built from round, open-parenthesis forms. Azonix excels at constant-width, commanding lines, while the body's tall middle band gives running text a stocky, sturdy look.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-vai: Azonix looks drawn with a round-tipped pen, commanding and crisp. Below it, approachable Noto Sans Vai forms words as solid blocks, with generous space between curve ends and stems.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-traditional-nu: Noto Traditional Nushu reads like a broad-nibbed pen that never curls shut. Page after page, its bowls fill the line, approachable and neutral, while Azonix keeps every downstroke free of calligraphic swell.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-readex-pro: Professional through and through, Readex Pro has broad gaps at its terminals. Its calm weight never wavers from word to word, so text unspools smoothly under Azonix's commanding headings.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-sarpanch: Azonix draws commanding, round bowls that never swell or thin. Up top it excels at crisp wide-mouthed lettering, whereas Sarpanch does its best with an open-mouthed e and a compact ascender gap.
